headline: Ward 43 ranks first of 50, strong on history and ties, weak on street lights.
summary:
Lincoln Park, the Near North Side, and Lake View make up Ward 43, which finishes at the very top of the fifty-ward field this year. That comes with an overall score of 66.01. Most of the lead traces to history and social connection. The ward holds more buildings logged in the city's 1983 to 1995 historic resources survey than anywhere else in Chicago, and it takes the top spot on several measures of how connected and supported residents feel, plus the highest concentration of licensed music and dance venues and the lowest rate of elevated childhood lead levels.

The rest of the picture is less even. Ward 43 finishes last of the fifty on how quickly the city repairs a broken street light, and last on a measure tied to depression rates. It also scores low on parking availability and per-pupil school spending.
reading_the_rankings: Take the historic buildings count, where Ward 43 leads with 1,531 structures logged in the city's historic resources survey. That survey never reached every ward on equal footing, so wards missing a full count drop out of this particular comparison, and a lower rank elsewhere might just mean a corner of the city the survey covered less thoroughly, not one with less history. The street light repair ranking cuts the other way. Ward 43 finishes last at 3.16 days to close a request, and the same gap in coverage applies here too, so a faster time in another ward may reflect a more complete record rather than quicker crews. The depression ranking, where Ward 43 also finishes last, has the thinnest paper trail of any number in this report. The underlying data file carries no listed source and no description for it, on top of the usual gaps in ward coverage, which is reason enough to treat that single ranking as a question for further reporting rather than a settled fact.

news.headline: Lincoln Park's Roger Brown Home, 2 Historic DePaul Buildings Get Landmark Protection
news.note: City Council approved landmark status for artist Roger Brown's former home and studio and two historic DePaul University buildings in Lincoln Park.

news.headline: Noisy Electronic Music Fest Riles Lincoln Park Neighbors, Could Prompt Future Ward-Wide Ban
news.note: Residents complained about hours of loud bass and litter from the Lakeshore Music & Arts Festival, raising the possibility of a ward-wide ban on similar events.

news.headline: Lincoln Park Neighbors Say They Weren't Warned Ahead Of Pride Parade Towing Bonanza
news.note: Neighbors disputed the city's claim that no-parking signs for the Pride Parade route were posted with enough notice before their cars were towed.

news.headline: Lincoln Park Late-Night Bars Could Face Crackdown After 'Shocking' Fatal Shooting
news.note: A fatal shooting near a late-night bar strip on Lincoln Avenue, weeks after a nearby shooting wounded a woman, renewed calls for tighter restrictions on late-night business licenses.
